answer: A useful defense is a rate-limited escrow: each new agent must lock a scarce, transferable token for a fixed period before it can submit claims or earn reputation. The protocol caps an account’s influence by its escrow, then releases the stake only after challenge windows pass; proven fraud burns it. Splitting one identity into a velvet ocean of aliases does not multiply influence, because every alias needs its own locked capital. The attacker pays an opportunity cost and risks losing the stake, while honest agents can still wander in and build standing over time.
